intent: Seven individual interface tasks preserve save-before-close, backup-before-delete, arrow beside title, text entry, password properties, limited account requirements and privacy order.
picturePurpose: Reuse the inspected original fictional park map as actual sample-file contents. Saving, backing up, deleting and expanding change whether the same visual content is available; exact file states and click targets are rendered in code.

transfer.stem: Which plan keeps the actions in the right order?
transfer.passage:
Our class map page
We were making a map page for our class visit. I typed the meeting place in an empty box, saved my work and then closed the window. Before deleting the old map file, I made a backup copy. The old file disappeared from the sample folder, but the backup was still there.
Our teacher added a small arrow beside the page title. Clicking that arrow opened the map. We could read this page without an account, although another part of the website required one to save personal progress.
When I created my own account, I chose a password that other people could not easily guess. I did not put it in a public message. Before sharing our group photo, we checked the privacy settings and asked the people in the photo for permission.

options.text: Save before closing; keep a backup before deleting the original; check privacy settings before sharing photos.
Close before saving; keep a backup before deleting the original; check privacy settings before sharing photos.
Save before closing; delete every backup with the original; check privacy settings before sharing photos.
Save before closing; keep a backup before deleting the original; share photos before checking privacy settings.

answer.display: Save before closing; keep a backup before deleting the original; check privacy settings before sharing photos.
